requirements.title: Restore Ad Access on Original Account

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Shadan
Before hiring, I wanted to confirm you can help with my exact issue.

My Meta ad account cannot run ads. Meta first said I needed 2FA, but my personal account is already verified with two-step authentication, and I have successfully run Facebook ads in the past.

Meta support is now saying the issue is tied to my personal Facebook profile, not the ad account, due to “account integrity/authentic identity.”

Have you fixed this exact type of profile-level Meta restriction before?

value_updates.expected_behavior: Restore the ability to run Facebook ads from the original account by resolving the profile-level account integrity or identity restriction.

execution.observed_behavior: The original Meta ad account cannot run ads because Meta associates the restriction with the client's personal Facebook profile.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Okay, I spoke with Meta Support and they mentioned that since it has been more than 180 days since the user missed the deadline to restore the ad account. The restriction may be permanent.

But he support has forwarded the case to their internal team and created a support ticket. They will review the account and confirm whether the restriction can still be lifted or if it is permanent.

I also asked them about disabling Facebook's 2 factor authentication. They explained that Facebook's new "Advanced Protection" update no longer allows users to completely turn off 2 factor authentication once it has been enabled. This workaround used to work in the past but due to security improvements.. users can no longer fully disable 2FA after it has been activated.

ambiguity.description: Meta support indicated that the expired appeal period may make the restriction permanent, while an internal review remained pending to determine whether recovery was still possible.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: They mentioned on the call. It can't be fixed since it has been more than 180 days. Thats the appeal time.

execution.observed_behavior: Meta support reportedly concluded that the original account restriction could not be fixed because the 180-day appeal period had expired.
